name: yaml_parser_parse_block_sequence_entry
prose: Static libyaml parser state function. Returns 1 or 0 as follows. If first is nonzero it first does PEEK_TOKEN and then PUSHes that token's start_mark onto parser->marks without checking the PEEK_TOKEN result for NULL (a NULL token would be dereferenced); if the PUSH fails (parser->error set to YAML_MEMORY_ERROR) it returns 0; otherwise it skips the token. It then peeks the next token and returns 0 if none can be fetched. If that token is YAML_BLOCK_ENTRY_TOKEN it skips it and peeks again (return 0 if no token); if the new token is neither a block-entry nor a block-end token it pushes YAML_PARSE_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_STATE onto parser->states (return 0 if the push fails) and returns the result of yaml_parser_parse_node(parser, event, 1, 0); otherwise it sets parser->state to YAML_PARSE_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_STATE and returns the result of yaml_parser_process_empty_scalar (1 and an empty plain-scalar event, or 0 with YAML_MEMORY_ERROR if the one-byte malloc fails). If the token is YAML_BLOCK_END_TOKEN it sets parser->state to the popped parser->states entry, pops parser->marks, fills event with a sequence-end event using the token's marks, skips the token and returns 1. For any other token type it pops parser->marks and returns the result of yaml_parser_set_parser_error_context with problem "did not find expected '-' indicator" (an error return, 0).
note: Reviewer 1 (omits empty-scalar path) wrong: prose already had it, code lines 'else { parser->state = ...ENTRY_STATE; return yaml_parser_process_empty_scalar }'. Reviewer 2 right: with first!=0 the PEEK_TOKEN result is used as token->start_mark with no NULL check.

name: copy_event
prose: Test-helper in run-emitter.c. Switches on event_from->type and returns the value of the matching libyaml initializer called on event_to with data copied from event_from: yaml_stream_start_event_initialize, yaml_stream_end_event_initialize, yaml_document_start_event_initialize, yaml_document_end_event_initialize, yaml_alias_event_initialize, yaml_scalar_event_initialize, yaml_sequence_start_event_initialize, yaml_sequence_end_event_initialize, yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize or yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize. Those initializers return 1 on success and 0 on failure (for example allocation failure); copy_event passes that value through. For any other type value the default branch executes assert(1), which is a no-op, so control reaches the final return 0 and event_to is not touched by this function.
note: Reviewer (round 15) wrong: default branch is assert(1), which never fails, so the function falls out of the switch to 'return 0' (run-emitter.c copy_event default: / assert(1); / return 0). Original reviewer's 'opposite of stated' also wrong: prose already said 1 on success, 0 on failure.

name: main
prose: Test driver. First loop over argv from index 1: an argument equal to "-c" sets canonical, "-u" sets unicode; any other argument starting with '-' prints "Unknown option" and main returns 0 immediately. Every argument starting with '-' that was not rejected (i.e. -c and -u) is removed from argv by shifting and decrementing argc. If fewer than one file argument remains (argc < 2) it prints a usage line and returns 0. Otherwise for each file argument it prints a header, opens the file (assert(file)), initializes a parser and an emitter writing to a BUFFER_SIZE-byte in-memory buffer, then loops: yaml_parser_parse; if parsing fails it sets error=1 and leaves the loop; otherwise it stores a copy of the event with copy_event (assert(event_number < MAX_EVENTS) before the store, so up to MAX_EVENTS events fit) and emits the event, asserting that emit succeeds (or print_output, which returns 0 after printing the failure report, so the assert still fails). After the loop it deletes the parser and emitter and asserts fclose succeeded. If error is 0 it parses the emitted buffer again and for each event asserts the parse succeeded and compare_events matches the stored event, deleting each event. It then frees the stored events (events 0..event_number-1), prints "PASSED (length: <written>)" and calls print_output for the file; this PASSED line is printed even when the first pass stopped on a parse error (error=1, second pass skipped). After the last file main returns 0. All the asserts (fopen, initialize, copy_event, emit, parse, compare, fclose) abort the program when they fail, and compile to nothing if NDEBUG is defined.
note: Slice cut the head (main is at run-emitter.c:~214). Round-17 reviewer right: assert(event_number < MAX_EVENTS) permits exactly MAX_EVENTS events, prose said 'below MAX_EVENTS'. Round-15 reviewer's PASSED-after-parse-error point was already described.

name: __vsubss4
prose: Static device function (__DEVICE__) in the #else branch of '#if CUDA_VERSION >= 9000 && CUDA_VERSION < 9020' (that is, compiled when CUDA_VERSION is below 9000 or at least 9020; the other branch defines the same name as a call to __nv_vsubss4). name: #define __SURF_WRITE_V2(__op, __asm_dim, __asmtype, __type, __index_op_args, __index_args, __index_asm_args, __asm_op_args, __asm_args)
prose: Macro that generates a full specialization 'template <> struct __surf_read_write_v2<__op, __type>' whose static __device__ void __run(__type *__ptr, cudaSurfaceObject_t obj, <index args>, cudaSurfaceBoundaryMode mode) switches on mode. name: __DO_LANE_SCAN(uint32_t, uint32_t, u32)
prose: Generated function uint32_t __gpu_lane_scan_u32(uint64_t __lane_mask, uint32_t __x) from macro __DO_LANE_SCAN. It computes first = mask >> ctz(mask) and calls __gpu_read_first_lane_u32(mask, first & (first + 1)) (the argument is passed as uint32_t) to decide __divergent. If divergent it loops over the set bits of __lane_mask in ascending order, shuffling each active lane's x with __gpu_shuffle_idx_u32 and keeping a running accumulator so that the lane with that index gets accum + tmp (inclusive prefix). Otherwise it runs a log-step loop (step 1,2,4,... below __gpu_num_lanes()) adding the value shuffled from lane (lane_id - step) for lanes with lane_id >= step. It then returns __x. The result per lane is an inclusive prefix sum of the x values in uint32_t arithmetic (wrapping). Whether the non-divergent path gives the intended values for masks with gaps depends on the divergence test above; the code is written assuming the test classifies the mask correctly.

It decides __divergent as for the u32 version (via __gpu_read_first_lane_u64), then either loops over active lanes shuffling with __gpu_shuffle_idx_u64 (divergent branch) or runs the log-step shuffle loop (other branch), assigning into the 32-bit __x, and returns __x. The returned value is therefore the low 32 bits of the inclusive prefix sum; it is not a 64-bit sum.

name: __DO_LANE_SUM(uint32_t, u32)
prose: Generated function uint32_t __gpu_lane_sum_u32(uint64_t __lane_mask, uint32_t __x) from macro __DO_LANE_SUM. It computes the divergence flag as __gpu_lane_scan_u32 does (via __gpu_read_first_lane_u32). If divergent it returns __gpu_shuffle_idx_u32 of __gpu_lane_scan_u32(__lane_mask, __x) taken from lane 63 - clzll(__lane_mask) (the highest set bit of the mask), i.e. the scan value of the last active lane. Otherwise it runs a log-step loop adding the value shuffled from lane (step + lane_id), then returns __gpu_read_first_lane_u32(__lane_mask, __x). Arithmetic is uint32_t wrapping addition. Which lanes' values enter the sum in the non-divergent branch depends on the target shuffle's behavior for out-of-range indices.
